text: Why does the propositional truncation ∥A∥ provide a notion of 'mere existence' that matters in HoTT?
choices: Because it makes A into a set
Because stating ∥A∥ says A has an element WITHOUT committing to a specific one (no computational witness)
Because it collapses all types to propositions
Because ∥A∥ is equivalent to A for Kan complexes
explanation: ∥A∥ = 'there merely exists an element of A'. Unlike Σ(x:A).True (which provides a witness x), ∥A∥ erases the witness. This distinction is crucial for stating classical logic axioms constructively.
